title: Interpret robot LED colors to determine robot connection/task/fault status
summary: Use the robot’s two side LEDs to determine whether the robot is disconnected, searching for a label (task), idle (not in a task), or in a fault/low-battery state. When the LEDs are red, confirm the corresponding fault/low-battery information in the message panel.
when_to_use: When you need to quickly interpret a robot’s current connection/task/fault/low-battery state by observing its LED colors in the Robot Selection Overview view, and (if red) verify the related fault/low-battery details in the message panel.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for resolving the underlying fault/low-battery condition; it only helps you identify the state and confirm the message panel content when LEDs are red.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Observe the robot LEDs and map the observed color pattern to the documented robot state; when LEDs are red, confirm the corresponding fault/low-battery information in the message panel.
access_or_tools_needed: Visual access to the robot LEDs
Access to the message panel on the HMI to confirm fault/low battery when LEDs are red

access_required: Access to the RMS message panel (to view fault/low-battery information when LEDs are red)
system_preconditions: Robot LEDs are visible (robots have two LEDs on each side).
Message panel is available in the RMS UI.

visual_references.description: Robot Selection Overview frame showing robot LED color meanings (purple/blue/flashing blue/green/red) and the relationship that red fault/low-battery appears in the message panel.

steps.title: Locate the robot’s LEDs on the robot sides
steps.purpose: You must see the LED colors to determine the robot’s connection/task/fault status.
steps.instruction: Visually locate the robot’s LEDs. The robots have two LEDs on each side.
steps.expected_result: You can clearly observe the robot’s LED color/state (purple, blue, flashing blue, green, or red).
steps.healthy_condition: LED colors are visible and you can distinguish between solid blue vs flashing blue and solid green vs red.
steps.failure_condition: LED colors/states are not visible or cannot be distinguished (e.g., you cannot tell whether blue is flashing).

actions.label: Inspect robot LEDs
actions.exact_action: Locate the robot’s LEDs (robots have two LEDs on each side).

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot clearly observe the LED colors/states, stop and escalate for on-site assistance or further troubleshooting.

steps.title: Match the observed LED color/state to the documented robot status
steps.purpose: Convert the observed LED color pattern into a specific robot state (disconnected, task/searching for label, idle, fault/low battery).
steps.instruction: Compare the observed LED color/state to the documented meanings: Purple = robot disconnected; Blue/Flashing Blue = robot in task / searching for a label (flashing blue indicates looking for a label); Green = robot idle (not in a task); Red = robot has fault or low battery.
steps.expected_result: You identify which documented color pattern the robot matches: purple, blue/flashing blue, green, or red.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed LED state matches one of the documented patterns (purple/blue/flashing blue/green/red).
steps.failure_condition: The LED color/state does not match any documented color/state pattern.

actions.label: Map LED color to robot status
actions.exact_action: Identify which documented color pattern it matches: Purple (robot disconnected), Blue/Flashing Blue (robot in task/searching for label), Green (robot idle/not in a task), Red (fault or low battery).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the LED color does not match any documented color/state, stop and escalate.

steps.title: If LEDs are Blue or Flashing Blue, interpret as task/searching for a label
steps.purpose: Provide the correct operational interpretation for blue/flashing blue LED states.
steps.instruction: If the LEDs are Blue or Flashing Blue, interpret it as the robot is in task/searching for a label. Specifically, flashing blue indicates the robot is looking for a label.
steps.expected_result: Robot status is identified as “in task/searching for a label” (flashing blue = looking for a label).
steps.healthy_condition: LEDs are clearly blue or flashing blue and you can distinguish flashing blue from solid blue.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine whether the blue state is flashing blue vs solid blue.

actions.label: Interpret blue/flashing blue
actions.exact_action: If the LEDs are Blue or Flashing Blue, interpret it as the robot is in task/searching for a label (flashing blue indicates looking for a label).

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot distinguish flashing blue from solid blue, stop and escalate.

steps.title: If LEDs are Green, interpret as idle (not in a task)
steps.purpose: Provide the correct operational interpretation for green LED state.
steps.instruction: If the LEDs are Green, interpret it as the robot is idle (not in a task).
steps.expected_result: Robot status is identified as “idle/not in a task.”
steps.failure_condition: LEDs are not solid green or appear to be transitioning between colors.

actions.label: Interpret green
actions.exact_action: If the LEDs are Green, interpret it as the robot is idle (not in a task).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the LED state is ambiguous (e.g., not clearly solid green), stop and escalate.

steps.title: If LEDs are Red, interpret as fault or low battery and confirm in the message panel
steps.purpose: Red indicates fault/low battery; the message panel should show the corresponding information.
steps.instruction: If the LEDs are Red, interpret it as fault or low battery. Then open/inspect the RMS message panel and confirm that the corresponding fault/low-battery information appears there.
steps.expected_result: You identify the robot as “fault/low battery” from the red LEDs, and the message panel shows the corresponding fault/low-battery information.
steps.healthy_condition: LEDs are red, and the message panel contains the fault/low-battery details associated with the robot state.
steps.failure_condition: LEDs are red but the message panel does not show fault/low-battery information as described.

actions.label: Interpret red LEDs
actions.exact_action: If the LEDs are Red, interpret it as fault or low battery.

actions.label: Confirm in message panel
actions.exact_action: Open/inspect the message panel to confirm the fault/low-battery information appears.

stop_or_escalate_if: If LEDs indicate Red but the message panel does not show fault/low-battery information, stop and escalate.

success_criteria: You can state the robot’s status based on the observed LED color pattern (purple/blue/flashing blue/green/red).
When LEDs are red, you can confirm the fault/low-battery information appears in the message panel.
healthy_conditions: LED colors match one of the documented patterns (purple/blue/flashing blue/green/red).
For red LEDs, the message panel contains the fault/low-battery information.
failure_conditions: LED color/state does not match any documented color/state pattern.
LEDs indicate red, but the message panel does not show fault/low-battery information.
escalation_guidance: If the LED color/state does not match any documented pattern, stop and escalate.
If LEDs indicate red but the message panel does not show fault/low-battery information, stop and escalate.

screens_or_images.description: Robot Selection Overview frame containing the LED color-to-status mapping and the note that red fault/low battery appears in the message panel.

missing_details: The packet does not provide the exact UI navigation steps/click path to open the message panel; it only states that the message panel can be opened to view active errors/warnings and alarm history.
